news.title: Three signals shaping Australian international education ahead of AIEC 2026
news.summary_en: From slowing student growth and tighter visa settings to the rise of transnational education, Australia's international education sector is entering a new phase. Ahead of AIEC 2026, The PIE looks at five shifts likely to shape conversations on the ground.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Enroly: UK CAS issuance falls 24% as visa refusals jump 44%
news.summary_en: International student recruitment at UK universities has taken another hit, with CAS issuance down almost a quarter year-on-year and visa refusals climbing sharply, new Enroly data suggests.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Refugee student route aims to bring 40 students to UK universities in 2027
news.summary_en: A new safe and legal route for refugee students is aiming to bring 40 students to UK universities for September 2027, with around 15 institutions expected to take part in the first cohort.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Efekta expands Rwanda ELT program, training over 90k teachers
news.summary_en: AI-powered language learning platform Efekta has scaled up its one-year English language proficiency program in Rwanda to reach over 90,000 teachers.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: New study signals rethink of overseas education among India’s Gen Z
news.summary_en: Cost and visa concerns are tempering overseas ambitions, an Emeritus survey finds, as international programs in India appeal to students weighing where and how to pursue a global education.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Myanmar students flock to Germany, Thailand, Malaysia for visa, finance reasons
news.summary_en: Germany, Thailand and Malaysia are attracting students from Myanmar as political instability complicates international study plans.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: New Zealand to help more schools recruit international students
news.summary_en: New Zealand is investing up to NZ$2.5 million in a new support service designed to help more schools recruit, enrol and retain international students from 2027, as the government pushes ahead with ambitious international education growth targets.
news.author: Kim Martin
